items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: the other band with a young new piano player from Pittsburgh -- was Errol Garner and Slam Stewart was the leader... Clyde Hart on piano with us

ctx.x: Of course in this band with Ted Sturgis on bass, you playing drums; of course Don Byas was a great tenor saxophone player, like Ben Webster -- also a great tenor saxophone player, huh, Cliff?

However, the other band with a young new piano player from Pittsburgh -- was Errol Garner and Slam Stewart was the leader, and wonderfully talented Harold West on drums. He did lovely brush work, and utilized a new sound to me by accenting the heavy part with the stick and the bell with a large cymbal. A little of that rubbed off on me along the way.

With Slam, he injected great humor in our style, and of course Errol Garner was contributing his great new piano style, and Clyde Hart on piano with us, was a great underrated musician, also. Billie Holiday used him on some of her records and Don Byas, another one of a kind tenor
